clue.text: Freak has the occasional party

parts.note: the occasional thing is an odd one, here and there
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A strange character is someone who throws a party now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A freak is an eccentric, an unconventional person, which is what the word denotes.

clue.text: Flip over king, say, and queen, perhaps on a now obsolete coin

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it
flipping a playing card over turns it, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card
HM, Her Majesty, is how a queen may be styled

explanation.surface: Someone turns over a king and a queen while describing a coin no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king, say' and 'queen, perhaps' tempt you towards R or K; the king is a playing card, flipped over, and the queen is Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek monetary unit was replaced by the euro in 2002, so it is a coin now out of circulation.

clue.text: 17 place bottom on top of lap

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: the base of something is its bottom

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A runner arrives at the base at the start of a lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SWISS (from SWISS ARMY KNIFE), so the definition asks for a Swiss place.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a city in northern Switzerland on the Rhine, a Swiss location.

clue.text: Contents of a pack including drink — that's ironic, to say the least!

definitions.note: describes ironic understatement, the figure of speech asked for

indicators.note: including means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a pack of lies is a stock phrase, so lies are what such a pack contains
a tot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A remark about a pack holding a drink, made with deliberate understatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pack of lies' is the stock phrase that tells you what such a pack contains.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of speech is ironic understatement, as in saying 'not bad' for excellent.

clue.text: See 14
In time sell short — or pay back

indicators.note: In placed first means the next piece goes inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: short means the selling word loses its last letter

parts.note: to vend is to sell

explanation.surface: A trader who sells short in good time may hope to recover losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sell short' looks like stock-market jargon, but 'short' just trims the last letter of the selling word.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge, to repay it in kind.

clue.text: Gut feeling it's how teachers make money?

definitions.meaning: an instinctive sense that something is so
read as two words, teachers earn their living ...

explanation.walkthrough: Split into IN TUITION it describes where a tutor's earnings come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is knowing something by instinct, a hunch from the gut rather than reasoning.

clue.text: Roosevelt's initiatives exposed something slippery, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the phrase is spoken to give a near-identical sounding phrase

parts.note: a nude eel is a bare creature notorious for being slippery

explanation.surface: A political programme revealed a slippery customer, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW DEAL was Franklin D. Roosevelt's 1930s American recovery programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1930s American economic recovery programmes of Franklin D. Roosevelt went by this name.

clue.text: Constant return generated a little money to feed one side of Manchester

indicators.note: to feed means these letters are put inside the football word

parts.note: Manchester United is one of the city's two football teams

indicators.note: generated signals the preceding word's letters being produced in a new order

parts.note: p, a penny, is a small amount of British money

explanation.surface: A steady income stream helps fund one of Manchester's football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one side of Manchester' is the football club Manchester United; 'generated' scrambles 'return', and the penny follows it inside the club after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant goes on without a break, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Service block

definitions.meaning: a solid lump or block of material

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a Catholic church service and a large solid lump of matter.

clue.text: Lean outlines a number of points, personal, in film location

indicators.note: outlines means the lean word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to tilt is to lean
north, south and east are compass points
own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: The director David Lean sketches personal touches into a film location.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Lean' points to the film director David Lean, but here it is just a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, the centre of the American film industry.

clue.text: Characters representative of the 17 on trial, legs akimbo, as attendants off piste?

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland, the country of 17 (SWISS)

indicators.note: legs akimbo are splayed out of line, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Swiss officials on trial sit with legs splayed, acting as attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'akimbo' rearranges TRIAL LEGS into ALET GIRLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Young women employed to cook and clean in ski chalets work away from the slopes, off piste.

clue.text: Elgin having lost marbles, horse half gone, revealing habit

indicators.note: having lost one's marbles means gone mad, so these letters are scrambled
half gone means only one half of the horse word remains

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Lord Elgin, without his famous marbles and down a horse, shows his true habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles are Greek sculptures in the British Museum. 'having lost marbles' rearranges ELGIN to NEGLI; 'half gone' cuts GEEGEE to GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a sheer, often revealing nightgown, and habit means clothing.

clue.text: Building is sensational pad, this 17 edifice

indicators.note: building means constructing the phrase that follows from its letters

explanation.surface: A grand pad described as sensational is a building in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges IS SENSATIONAL PAD into the answer. 17 is SWISS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Geneva palace houses the United Nations Office, a notable building in Switzerland.

clue.text: No one with hair on end underwrites a claim

indicators.note: underwrites means written beneath, so the reversed run sits below the a in a down clue
stood on end in a down clue, these pieces read upwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An insurer backing a claim, with someone's hair standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on end' turns NO I TRESS into SSERTION, written under A.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident statement or claim that something is true.

clue.text: See 12
Second dark man, fool, laid back in embrace of the missus, as multitasker

indicators.note: in embrace of means held inside the following piece

parts.note: the missus is a casual term for one's wife

indicators.note: laid back means these pieces are set down in reverse order

parts.note: inky means dark as ink
Mr, Mister, is the title for a man
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A gloomy man and a fool lounge in the arms of the wife, juggling tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' looks like relaxed but reverses the dark, man and fool pieces; 'in embrace of' sets them inside the wife after her first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-handled pocket tool has many blades and gadgets, so it handles many tasks at once.

clue.text: Power demonstrated by a hollow tyrant cutting pay

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the pay word

parts.note: a wage is pay

indicators.note: hollow means the inner letters are removed, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A tyrant without substance shows his power by slashing wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' keeps only the outside letters of tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattage is electrical power measured in watts.

clue.text: See 17
Mexican state currency protecting the queen, say

indicators.note: protecting means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: the yuan is the currency of China
a queen is a female cat, an example of one

explanation.surface: A nation's money is used to shield its monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the name for a female cat, not a monarch here.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucatán is a state of Mexico on the peninsula of the same name.

clue.text: Disapprove of loud argument over French veto

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier pieces sit above the next

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a row is a noisy argument
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A noisy quarrel erupts over a French refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown on something is an idiom meaning to regard it with disapproval.

clue.text: Feature about work, one of his taking a minute?

definitions.text: one of his taking a minute?
definitions.note: points to a composer by a famous piece of his: the Minute Waltz

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
op, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A face is described around a work, with one of something lasting a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's Minute Waltz is popularly thought to take a minute to play; the definition describes him by that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish composer wrote the Waltz in D flat, nicknamed the Minute Waltz, reputedly playable in sixty seconds.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller *** cool!

parts.note: three asterisks look like a row of stars
hip means cool, fashionable

explanation.surface: A space traveller is rated three stars and called cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisks are a picture of three stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft for interstellar travel journeys vast distances between stars.

clue.text: Barmy notice that may be 17?

definitions.note: describes something likely to be Swiss

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy, barmy
to clock is slang for to notice

explanation.surface: Someone says a crazy sign might be Swiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SWISS; 'barmy' is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo clocks are strongly associated with Switzerland and the Black Forest, so one may be Swiss.

clue.text: See 24
Reused manuscript most bleached, devils inscribed

indicators.note: inscribed means written inside the bleached word

parts.note: palest means most bleached of colour
imps are little devils

explanation.surface: Faded old writing with demons drawn on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribed' writes the devils inside the bleached word after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment scraped and written over again, with traces of the old text showing.

clue.text: Noise primarily in boor — or boar?

definitions.text: Noise primarily in boor — or boar?

indicators.note: in means the first letter of noise sits inside the boor word

parts.note: an oik is a British slang word for a boorish person

indicators.note: primarily means taking just the first letter

explanation.surface: Is that grunt from an uncouth man or a wild pig?
explanation.walkthrough: OIK is British slang for a crude, uncultured person.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting noise made by a pig such as a boar.

clue.text: 17 location in 17 centre for Italian sculptor

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital, a place in Switzerland

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: 17 is the answer SWISS

explanation.surface: A Swiss place and a Swiss centre are linked to an Italian artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SWISS; its central letter is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the leading Italian Baroque sculptor, famed for St Peter's Square.

clue.text: Difficulty with infusion of one's own blood going this way and that

indicators.note: an infusion puts something inside, so the relatives go into the difficulty word

parts.note: a snag is a difficulty or hitch
one's own blood means one's family, kin

explanation.surface: A problem arises when a patient receives a transfusion of his own blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with infusion of' sets the relatives inside the difficulty word, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaking means winding or meandering, like a snake's path.
